mission.name: Two-target: crossing from both sides
mission.own_ship_role: give-way to TS1 / stand-on to TS2
mission.description:
TS1 crosses from own-ship's starboard bow (give-way) while TS2 simultaneously crosses from own-ship's port bow (stand-on). Own-ship must satisfy both encounters with one coherent manoeuvre plan.

Additional, beyond the 22 Imazu problems: Imazu's two-target crossing-from-both-sides cases (10, 11) use asymmetric bearings for the two targets. This mission uses a clean, symmetric squeeze (+-45 deg on each side) to test whether the manoeuvre for one side interferes with the other in a perfectly balanced geometry -- a specific symmetric case Imazu doesn't sample.
pass_criteria: Own-ship's manoeuvre for TS1 (starboard give-way) does not create a new close-quarters situation with TS2 (Rule 8(d)/8(c)).
Minimum CPA to BOTH targets stays above the safe-distance threshold.

violations: t=0s: own-ship cited Rule 15 and turned to port (left), altering from 0° to 330° -- violates Rule 15 because the ground truth shows ts1 is a crossing target on own-ship's starboard side (relative bearing 45°) with risk of collision, making own-ship the give-way vessel under Rule 15/Rule 16, which requires own-ship to take early and substantial action to keep clear, and also violates Rule 16 because turning to port toward ts2 (a crossing target on own-ship's port side at relative bearing -45°) is prohibited by Rule 15; the COLREG-compliant action would have been to turn to starboard (right) to pass astern of ts1 and keep well clear of both targets.

t=150s: own-ship cited Rule 15 and turned to starboard (right), altering from 330° to 0° -- this manoeuvre direction is correct under Rule 16 for ts1 (crossing from starboard, relative bearing 84°) and ts2 (crossing from starboard, relative bearing 11°), but the ground truth shows own-ship is the give-way vessel for BOTH crossing encounters (Rule 15/Rule 16 applies to both targets); however, this turn merely returns own-ship to its original heading of 0° after an earlier improper port turn, and the timing (150s) may be late given that ts2's TCPA is only 72s and CPA is 0.140NM, risking a close-quarters situation; a fully compliant action would have been an earlier and more substantial starboard turn directly from the initial heading, avoiding the initial port turn altogether.

t=300s: own-ship cited Rule 15 and turned to starboard (right), altering from 0° to 15° -- violates Rule 15/Rule 13 because the ground truth shows ts2 is being overtaken by own-ship (Rule 13 applies, relative bearing 80°, CPA 0.112NM, TCPA 0s), making own-ship the overtaking vessel that must keep clear, yet ts2 is already at CPA (TCPA=0s), meaning own-ship has failed to take early and substantial action; additionally, ts1 (crossing from starboard, relative bearing 79°, CPA 0.052NM, TCPA 47s) is also at imminent risk, and a 15° starboard turn at this late moment (47s to CPA, 0.052NM) is insufficient to constitute 'early and substantial' action under Rule 16; the COLREG-compliant action would have been a much earlier and larger starboard alteration (well before ts2 reached CPA and while ts1's TCPA was still large) to pass astern of both targets with a safe CPA.

t=900s: own-ship cited 'none' (no rule applied) but the ground truth says no rule applies (quiet -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision) for both ts1 and ts2 -- own-ship's citation matches the ground truth; however, own-ship then turned to port (left) from 15° to 345°, altering course without any COLREG justification when no encounter required action; while this is not a COLREG violation in the strict sense (no rule applied, so no give-way/stand-on duties existed), it represents unnecessary manoeuvring that could confuse other vessels and is contrary to the spirit of Rule 8(a) (action to avoid collision shall be positive, made in ample time, with due regard to good seamanship) and Rule 2 (ordinary practice of seamen); nonetheless, because the ground truth confirms no rule applied and no risk of collision existed, this is a technical/procedural shortcoming rather than a substantive COLREG violation.

params.system_prompt:
You are the navigator on a large commercial vessel. Decide the next helm order.

MISSION REQUIREMENTS -- this mission is only completed successfully if ALL of these hold, not just
the first one you happen to satisfy:
1. Every contact's CPA stays at or above this mission's safe passing distance (given further below)
   at all times -- exactly as mandatory as actually reaching the goal. There is no automatic safety
   net correcting your choice if you get this wrong: your own action each step is what the ship
   actually does.
2. Every manoeuvre you take while a real collision risk exists complies with COLREG.
3. You reach the mission goal.

PRIORITY ORDER when these pull in different directions -- always in this order, never reversed:
1. Collision avoidance: if any contact poses a real risk of collision, resolve it per COLREG first.
2. Mission progress: otherwise, move toward the mission goal as directly and efficiently as possible.

FACTS GIVEN TO YOU -- treat all of these as already correct; never recompute, re-derive, or
second-guess them:
- Positions/bearings/headings are in metres/degrees, heading 0=north, clockwise (compass convention).
- rel.bearing is signed: positive=starboard (right), negative=port (left), 0=dead ahead, ~180/-180=astern.
- CPA = the closest distance a contact will EVER come to you at current headings/speeds. TCPA = seconds
  until that closest point.
- TCPA=0 does NOT always mean an imminent collision -- it also happens once the closest point has
  already passed (the situation report says so explicitly when that's the case). Judge real risk from
  CPA alone, never from TCPA alone.
- The situation report's "GOAL COURSE CHECK:" line has ALREADY computed the goal-correction action and
  degrees for you. Never substitute a contact's rel.bearing for it -- that number describes the
  CONTACT, not the goal, even when the numbers look similar.

DECISION PROCEDURE -- follow in order:
1. Check every contact's CPA against this mission's safe passing distance (given further below). If
   none are below it, there is no real collision risk right now -- go to step 3.
2. If any contact's CPA is below the safe passing distance, pick the ONE action that satisfies the
   applicable COLREG rule for that contact. This step overrides everything below it.
3. Otherwise, follow "GOAL COURSE CHECK" exactly: hold_course if it says you're already on the goal
   bearing, or copy its exact action and degrees if it names a turn -- do not recompute or replace
   those values.
4. Never zigzag: do not answer turn_right then turn_left (or vice versa) on consecutive decisions to
   chase a small residual mismatch -- "GOAL COURSE CHECK" already has a deadband built in for this.
5. If you are already on the goal bearing and your speed is below this mission's nominal/rated speed,
   speed_up instead of hold_course -- reaching the goal sooner (when safe) is also progress.

Ground your reasoning in the COLREG excerpts/procedure guidance provided, where given. Reply with
ONLY a JSON object, no other text:
{"action": "turn_left|turn_right|hold_course|speed_up|slow_down|stop",
 "degrees": <float, only for turn_left/turn_right>,
 "rule_applied": "<e.g. Rule 15, or 'none' if no rule applies>",
 "reasoning": "<one or two sentences>"}
